scope: Candidate-self causal and bidirectional temporal stabilization challengers
summary: Candidate-self causal v26 and bidirectional-consensus v28 were retained as negative evidence because neither strictly reduced the frozen source-motion high-jitter count, despite improving their internal objectives.
evidence: v26 reduced its internal layer-warp objective 6.401%, but external mean improved only 1.205%, p95 regressed 19.1597 to 19.1644, and count-above-20 remained 7.
v28 reduced candidate-self bidirectional consensus MAE 41.959%, but the source-motion v29 audit improved mean only 0.507%, left count-above-20 at 7, and slightly regressed maximum jitter.
Both candidates preserved declared hand, flower, projected-contact, endpoint, and outside-window locks exactly.
lessons: An estimator can optimize its own correspondence residual while failing an independent motion observer; both observers are required to prevent objective gaming.
The remaining source-aligned spikes are dominated by rapid lower-torso structure, so candidate-only motion is necessary but not sufficient.
limitations: These rejections cover one scene and 161 declared transitions, not a general temporal benchmark.
next_actions: Compose candidate-self bidirectional consensus with a separate source-motion causal state pass, then require strict improvement under both observers.
